pieces.text:
The cotton herds drift slow across the blue,
Like lazy thoughts that refuse to be known.
They mimic peaks of snow or mountain view,
Yet hold no weight and claim no earthly throne.
The vapor swells in bloated, puffy mass,
A borrowed shape that borrows light from sun.
They watch the seasons shift and shadows pass,
With no intent to stay or be undone.
But look how tight the edges curl and fray,
A tattered hem where summer heat has bitten.
They do not mean to drift and fade away,
But cling to thermals while the day is smitten.
Each lumpy pile pretends to touch the sky,
While waiting for the wind to tell a lie.
